instructions: See docs/ratings.md. Give every season a rating on the absolute scale. Rate the player that season, never their career.

seasons.note: Sixteen years old and a cameo player; rated as the unformed teenager, not the England international he became.
West Ham’s captain at twenty and comfortably their best player in a relegation season.
Eight goals in nineteen starts as he began to add end product to the dribbling.
Chelsea’s players’ player of the year in a title season; the dribbling finally married to end product.
Three starts before a broken ankle in January ended the season; the football before it was the 2005/06 player.
Ruptured a cruciate in January; fourteen starts.
Back from the knee but no longer trusted as a starter; a yard of the close control had gone.
Ever-present at 23 and, on reading of the game and recovery pace, close to the best defender in the division; the knee that later limited him had not yet done so.
Four starts: the knee has taken his season, not his ability. Rated as the defender he still was on the days he could play.
Six league starts. Still an elite defender in the games his knees allowed, but that is what the season was.
Breakthrough at 20: 25 goals and 11 assists as a first-choice forward after a raw, in-and-out first season.
Nine starts: hernia and knee trouble wrecked the season.
Three goals in a relegation season. The output collapsed; on the evidence of 1997/98 and of Celtic afterwards, the player did not collapse with it.
One league goal at Chelsea, often played wide and out of position. Rated as the forward he still was, not as the season looked.
Six years at Celtic in between; back in England at thirty-two he is a bench forward with the touch intact and nothing else.
The blocking, front-foot half of the treble season’s centre-back pair; no distribution to speak of, but as good a pure defender as there was in the division that year.
Fifteen starts; injuries and the arrival of younger legs.
Rated as the 20-year-old breaking through after two broken legs, not the England player he became.
The rise from the 1992/93 rating spans two seasons lost to broken legs; he came back a materially better player and was an ever-present for a side that finished third.
Five starts before a knee injury he never properly recovered from; the pace never came back.
The screening midfielder of the treble side; positionally outstanding and a far better passer than the role suggested.
A first Premier League season at 23 and immediately Villa’s best defender; strong, quick across the ground, entirely without frills.
Eleven league goals at nineteen in a Champions League semi-final side.
Nine goals in a relegated side while also being asked to play in midfield; the ability was well above the results.
Fifteen starts and a badly broken leg in February; already being used away from the forward line.
Twenty-six starts and no goals, converted into a central midfielder he was never quite good enough on the ball to be.
Title winner and an England call-up; his peak.
Cruciate injury, ten starts.
His best season - 19 goals and 15 assists carrying a poor side.
A flat year under Souness; the same ability, much less of it applied.
Nine starts at 30, and physically finished as a first-choice player.
Sixteen years old and physically unready, but already a competent top-flight substitute — rated as the player he was then, not the England midfielder he became.
Seven goals and twelve assists, PFA Young Player of the Year and an England starter; the season he stopped being a prospect.
Thirty-nine, sixteen seasons after the peak above, and still a genuine rotation option rather than a ceremonial squad number — which is what a 74 means.
Record fee for a defender, moving to Newcastle in March 1994.
Ever-present and in the PFA Team of the Year in a promoted Fulham side; positionally excellent, quietly good at everything and spectacular at nothing.
Twenty-nine and the most complete season of a very even career; a Champions League and FA Cup winning right-back at his peak.
Thirty-three, a year in Spain in between, and a regular for a Portsmouth side relegated in administration.
Moved to Portsmouth in January; the same finisher at both clubs.
Moved to Portsmouth in January; the same finisher at both clubs.
Returned to Tottenham in January; the same finisher at both clubs.
Returned to Tottenham in January; the same finisher at both clubs.
Eighteen league goals in a side that qualified for the Champions League; the sharpest season of his career.
Moved to Tottenham in August; the same player at both clubs.
Moved to Tottenham in August; the same player at both clubs.
Nine starts; injuries, and better midfielders arriving around him.
Nine starts; out of favour under Moyes rather than physically finished.
Restored as a first pick at 34 in the side that finished fourth.
Thirty-five starts at twenty in Wigan’s first top-flight season; the left foot and the delivery were already the best part of him.
A first Everton season spent behind Lescott; thirteen starts, and no worse a footballer for it.
Thirty-seven starts and eight assists at twenty-four; Everton’s settled first choice and among the better attacking left-backs in the division.
Thirty-eight starts, five goals and eleven assists from left back; the season he became the best in the country in the position after Cole.
His peak season: the best left-back in the league that year on delivery and set pieces, if never dominant defensively.
Three seasons on, and two of them in the second tier where he became a far better player; England caps followed in 1999.
Relegated with nineteen points and the captain of it; the level dropped with the side.

Fifteen goals conceded in 35 games and a record clean-sheet run. Positioning, handling and shot-stopping were all at the very top of the world game that season, which is what puts him in the 90s at 22 rather than the 80s.
The fractured skull at Reading in October cost him three months and, on the evidence of everything after it, a little of the command that had made him unbeatable at twenty-two.
Thirty-four starts in a Double-winning season and back close to his best, though not back to the 2004/05 level.
Breakout year: pace and composure that earned a World Cup place and a record fee for a defender.
Joined Liverpool in September 1994; the same player at both clubs.
Joined Liverpool in September 1994; the same player at both clubs.
Never settled as a Liverpool centre-back, and the confidence on the ball went with it.
Four years on from his last rated season and now 31, an ever-present centre-half for a Sunderland side relegated with 19 points — evidence about the side, not the player.
Eleven assists and an England call-up at 20; the left foot and the delivery were already top-flight quality, the rest of the game was not.
A broken foot in September cost him most of the season.
Ever-present, nine goals and an established England place; the running and the finishing finally caught up with the delivery.
A metatarsal injury kept him out until December of his first Villa season.
Seven starts; a knee injury cost him most of the season.
Nineteen starts for the eleven-point Derby side; being one of its better players says nothing good about the level.
Ever-present for a West Ham side that finished fifth; the best sustained run of his career.
Displaced by David James after twelve starts.
Nine assists in a West Brom side that survived from bottom at Christmas; good delivery, ordinary everything else.
Thirty league goals and the European Golden Boot, but the profile is a sharp penalty-box finisher rather than a complete forward — deliberately kept below the Shearer and Cole anchors.
Fourteen goals rather than thirty; defenders had worked him out and Sunderland created less.
Six goals in a side relegated with nineteen points.
Thirteen goals in twenty-eight starts at Southampton; the finishing was still sharp in a much lesser role.
Thirty-six and a substitute, but four goals in 434 minutes; the finishing outlasted everything else about him.
Ever-present for a relegated Norwich but a genuinely good shot-stopper who went on to play for England — rated on the ability, not the goals conceded.
A first West Ham season after most of the previous one was lost to a back injury.
Ever-present again and England’s first choice by the end of it; a very good shot-stopper behind a defence that gave him little help.
Rated as the raw, wasteful teenager he was at Arsenal, not the Fulham player of 2005.
Nine goals from the left at 25 - the season the pace and directness finally came with an end product.
Split between Fulham and West Ham in January; the same player at both, and one league goal at either.
Split between Fulham and West Ham in January; the same player at both, and one league goal at either.
A long-serving top-flight starter with essentially no attacking contribution; a 1990s lower-half floor player who would not be in a modern squad.
Captain of the FA Cup winners and still the best defender at the club.
Five starts at 37.
Twenty-one, six goals, and relegation with Coventry; the pace was already among the most destructive in the division, the decision-making was not.
A step up rather than a transformation - the same pace applied in a Newcastle side that finished fourth, with nine goals and far better service.
Thirteen goals in twenty-two starts; the pace and the finishing at their most aligned.
Seven starts in an injury-wrecked season.
Moved to Manchester City in January; the same player at both clubs.
Moved to Manchester City in January; the same player at both clubs.
Ten goals and eight assists at thirty, reinvented off the left where the pace still counted.
An 18-year-old who was already the best defender in a European-qualifying side and capped by England within the season — rated on what he could do then, which was a lot.
Fourteen starts across a season disrupted by the assault trial; the football, when he played it, was that of 1999/00.
Excellent at both clubs, before and after the January move to Newcastle; at 22 the best English centre-half of his age and a Real Madrid target on merit.
Excellent at both clubs, before and after the January move to Newcastle; at 22 the best English centre-half of his age and a Real Madrid target on merit.
Back from two lost years in Madrid and immediately Middlesbrough’s best player; the reading of the game was intact, the body less so.
Moved to Tottenham in January; the same player at both clubs.
Moved to Tottenham in January; the same player at both clubs.
Thirty-four starts, the only fully fit season of his post-Madrid career, and level with his Leeds peak.
Nine starts at 33 after Rangers, and plainly finished as a top-flight starter.
Joined Sheffield Wednesday in January 1998.
Joined Sheffield Wednesday in January 1998.
Moved to Bolton in January; the same player at both clubs.
Moved to Bolton in January; the same player at both clubs.
Thirty-two and at a relegated Norwich; below top-flight standard by this point.
Lost the shirt to Antti Niemi midway through the season.
Thirty-six, split between a Wolves loan and Southampton; the same keeper at both clubs.
Thirty-six, split between a Wolves loan and Southampton; the same keeper at both clubs.
Eleven assists from wide in a first English season; an Australia regular and a Champions League player with Feyenoord, athletic and two-footed.
Three starts at 34; the ability had gone before the appearances did.
Three starts at 36.
Still excellent and the main reason Everton stayed up, though past the late-1980s peak that sits outside this file.
Thirty-eight and finished; twelve starts before being dropped.
